tests.note: for anglophone listeners; fails a francophone listener

note: RPM year-end Top 100 of 1970 read from the scanned issue. Only one francophone song sourced (Ordinaire, tied to 1970 by its Sopot prize, no chart position found); Quebec palmarès data for 1970 not reachable.

RPM year-end list for 1971 could not be retrieved; ranking rests on weeks at number one, discography peaks and two weekly RPM issues. Foreign picks are the longest-running number ones (ties at 2-3 weeks broken arbitrarily). Francophone songs come from RPM's own French Canadian Top Ten / RPM 100 of 25 Dec 1971.

RPM year-end list for 1972 could not be retrieved; ranking rests on weeks at number one, discography peaks and weekly RPM issues (8 Jul and 30 Dec 1972). Foreign picks are the longest-running number ones. Francophone songs come from RPM's weekly French Canadian Top Ten (scan OCR, titles normalised).

RPM year-end Top 100 of 1973 read from the scanned issue. Only one francophone song sourced: J'entends frapper (1972 single, described as Quebec's best-selling 45; its exact peak year, late 1972 vs 1973, is not confirmed).

RPM year-end list for 1974 could not be retrieved (only its number one, Seasons in the Sun, is confirmed). Ranking rests on weeks at number one and discography peaks; the foreign picks are number ones with 2-3 weeks on top, ties broken arbitrarily. Only one francophone song sourced.

RPM year-end Top 200 of 1975 read from the scanned issue (ranks 101-200 partly garbled). Francophone songs have no chart positions: Gens du pays and Un peu plus haut are tied to the 24 June 1975 Mont-Royal concert, the Beau Dommage title to its 1975 single release.

RPM year-end Top 200 of 1976 read from the scanned issue. The two francophone songs have no chart positions: tied to 1976 by single release (Beau Dommage) and by Wikipedia's description of Boule Noire's first hit.

Thin evidence. RPM year-end list for 1977 could not be retrieved (only its number one is confirmed); no Canadian act topped the RPM singles chart in 1977. Home list rests on Juno Single of the Year nominees, discography peaks and country number ones; foreign picks are the longest-running number ones (2-week ties broken arbitrarily). No francophone song could be sourced for this year.

RPM year-end list for 1978 could not be retrieved (only its number one, Night Fever, is confirmed). Ranking rests on weeks at number one, Juno nominees, discography peaks and country number ones. Only one francophone song sourced (Heureux d'un printemps, described as a rapid success in 1978; no chart position).

RPM year-end list for 1979 could not be retrieved (only its number one, The Logical Song, is confirmed). Home list rests on one RPM number one, Juno Single of the Year nominees (1980 ceremony), discography peaks and country number ones; disco titles have no chart position sourced. Only one francophone song sourced (Le monde est stone, cited for Fabienne Thibeault's 1979 Félix awards; no chart position).
